lines.say: Final Fantasy was called Final for a reason. Or at least, that's the story.
It was made by Square, and directed by Hironobu Sakaguchi.
Its working title was Fighting Fantasy, but that name already belonged to a series of gamebooks.
Composer Nobuo Uematsu said Final meant Sakaguchi would quit if it flopped, and Square was facing possible bankruptcy.
Sakaguchi later said any word starting with F would have been fine.
You pick four heroes at the start, from six classes, and you're stuck with them for the whole game.
Its programmer, Nasir Gebelli, even added a hidden sliding puzzle that was never in the plan.
Square shipped 520,000 copies in Japan at first. By 1994, about 1.3 million had sold worldwide.
lines.cap: Square shipped 520,000 copies in Japan at first. By 1994, about 1.3 million had sold worldwide.

lines.say: So it wasn't final at all. The series is still going today.
